summary: Chelan County, WA 24-ft pole L-4 lookout built 1933 and removed in the 1950s; its converted garage still stands on the summit, now a drive-up campground per WillhiteWeb.

facts.design: 24-foot pole L-4 tower with an accompanying garage
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1950s; the garage, converted to Aircraft Warning Service living quarters in 1942, still stands on the summit per the register and WillhiteWeb

access.note: Drive-up summit campground per WillhiteWeb; road over Shady Pass from Entiat, conditions change; no closure described

events.note: 24-foot pole L-4 tower and an accompanying garage; WillhiteWeb says likely built by the CCC
Garage converted into Aircraft Warning Service living quarters
Aircraft Warning Service post activated March 20, 1942; deactivated July 1, 1943 (Seattle Filter Center)
Tower removed sometime in the 1950s; the register gives no exact year
Summit shown as a campground on the 1968 topo map; maps today show the same
Entiat Burn lightning fires in the Wenatchee National Forest; a note in the cabin dated 9/2/70 refers to the Shady Pass Fire and to charred land
Registered August 20, 2012 as US 1387, WA 287; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: The 24-foot tower is gone, but the garage converted to Aircraft Warning Service quarters still stands on the summit according to the register and WillhiteWeb

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe the tower as removed in the 1950s, while WillhiteWeb says the converted garage remains on the summit. Both are true of different structures, so the record is partial rather than gone.

notes_for_editor: The register and firelookout.com agree on the 1933 build and the 1950s removal, and WillhiteWeb confirms the 1942 conversion. The current condition of the garage, and the campground use, come only from WillhiteWeb (undated text and photos). The 1942-1943 Aircraft Warning Service dates come from Rex's page, which attributes them to an external listing. The 1970 fire note is a cabin sign quoted on WillhiteWeb; it does not say the summit burned. No source gives the exact year the tower came down. Correction proposed: the brief's status 'gone' ignores the surviving garage.
